conviction_note: The evidence offsets. On one side is an inferred revenue shortfall against a single-source Q3 bar, plus open items on the BNCC approval and the line-of-credit launch. On the other are a short that built to 7.4 days to cover, CEO open-market buying during Q3, and a stock at its 52-week low at about 4x the midpoint of the cut guide. After the lessons the findings sum to 0.0. p_up is 50 on an abs move of 11 (the name's median reaction is 10.8), so the scaled number is 0. The day this name moves is the full-year guide: reaffirmed or cut again.
bar: There are two bars. FY2026 company guide (cut 2026-08-10): revenue $600-625M, adjusted net income $115-130M, adjusted EPS $1.34-1.51 (https://s206.q4cdn.com/723382727/files/doc_news/OppFi-Reports-Second-Quarter-2026-Results-Record-Second-Quarter-Revenue-2026.pdf). FY consensus (S&P via stockanalysis, 4 analysts): revenue $611.4M, EPS $1.41, sitting inside the guide (https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/opfi/forecast/). The Q3 bar has ONE source: Earnings Whispers, EPS $0.41 on revenue $156.34M (https://www.earningswhispers.com/epsdetails/OPFI). Q3 sizes are therefore capped small. H1 revenue was $297.05M, so the guide implies H2 revenue of $303-328M, or about $151.5-164M a quarter.
positioning_check: FINRA short interest, from equibles (https://equibles.com/stocks/opfi/shortinterest). Settlement 2026-10-15: 4,283,126 shares, 7.40 days to cover, 5.0% of the 85.2M shares outstanding. Settlement 2026-09-30: 4.32M. Settlement 2026-07-31: 2.40M. The short has risen about 78% since before the August print. Free float is well below 85.2M: Class V was eliminated and every share is now Class A (10-Q cover, 85,208,247 shares at 2026-08-06), but the Schwartz entities hold a large block. The CEO's Form 4 alone shows about 26.9M shares direct plus indirect, so the short is a materially larger share of free float than 5%; I estimate low-to-mid teens, not sourced. No usable skew: the option chain is unusable (ATM spread 100% of mid, total open interest 626, put/call OI 0.35). Tape: -10.5% over 20 days, -52.2% from the 52-week high, 0.4% above the 52-week low.

findings.finding: This is my own arithmetic on primary-document metrics, not a company number. Q3 revenue is more likely $148-154M than the $156.3M single-source bar. Q2 2026 ended with receivables of $440.1M (+0.5% YoY), net originations of $212.0M (-9.3% YoY), retained originations -14.1% and yield of 132.4% (136.1% a year earlier). Q2 revenue of $145.2M implies average receivables of about $439M at that yield. Q3 2025 printed $155.1M revenue only after receivables grew about 10% in the quarter, from $437.8M to $481M, with originations +12.5%. To reach $156M at a 132% yield, average Q3 receivables need to be about $473M. That means roughly 15% quarter-on-quarter book growth while underwriting is being deliberately tightened.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: On 2026-08-10 revenue missed ($145.2M against about $156-160M) together with a guide cut, and the stock fell 24.9%. In Q1 2026 (2026-05-07), revenue of $152M with originations down 7% got +1.4%. A revenue miss on its own has not been isolated from guidance in this history.
findings.why_not_priced: The only Q3 revenue estimate I can find ($156.34M) is above what the Q2 book supports. If the market had marked Q3 down to the book, the published Q3 bar would sit near $150M. Instead the FY consensus ($611.4M) still sits on the guide midpoint, which needs H2 revenue of about $157M a quarter.
findings.independence: The Q3 2025 comparison comes from a different document: the company's Q3 2025 release, revenue $155.1M, receivables $481M (https://investors.oppfi.com/news/news-details/2025/OppFi-Reports-Record-Quarterly-Revenue-Net-Income-and-Adjusted-Net-Income-and-Increases-Full-Year-Guidance/default.aspx). The 8-K presentation confirms the tightening language: 'Deliberate credit tightening and moderated originations' (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001818502/000181850226000073/a2026q2earningspresentat.htm). Against this finding: the $75M term loan drawn 2026-09-15 is earmarked for receivables growth. All of this is an inference from the company's own metrics.

findings.finding: Credit is the line the cut guide rests on, and it was still deteriorating in Q2 despite tightening. Annualised net charge-offs were 52.3% of average receivables (43.5% a year earlier). NCO as a share of revenue was 39.5% (31.9% a year earlier). The fair-value mark on receivables was -$59.0M (-$42.2M a year earlier). On the Q4 2025 call management said summer vintages showed higher defaults, and those charge off in Q3. Q3 2025 printed NCO at 35.1% of revenue. A repeat of about 40% would keep pressure on adjusted net income, but the August guide was set with this credit picture in view.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 (NCO 52.3%) came with the guide cut: -24.9%. Q3 2025 (NCO 35.1% of revenue, only modestly higher) came with a guide raise: +3.8%.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: the guide was cut on it and the stock is at its 52-week low. What is not public is the Q3 NCO and the delinquency trend under Model 6.1. A stock already pricing worse credit would not have fallen another ~10% over 20 days. Its sign is uncertain, which is why this is sized small and inside the guide.
findings.independence: Q4 2025 call: summer-vintage defaults were higher (https://finance.yahoo.com/news/oppfi-q4-earnings-call-highlights-185825283.html). This shares the Q2 release and presentation with the revenue finding, but it is a different line (losses, not yield or book).

findings.finding: Enova's Q3 2026 release (2026-10-22) is the only subprime online-lender read that has printed since OppFi last spoke. Consolidated net charge-off ratio fell to 8.1% from 8.5% YoY, originations rose 31%, and management called credit 'stable'. 30+ day delinquency rose to 8.0% from 7.2%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No baseline record of OPFI reacting to an Enova print.
findings.why_not_priced: Enova printed after OppFi's last update, and OPFI kept drifting lower (it is down 9.6% in October). That suggests the read-across was not taken. It is a weak transmission: Enova's book is near-prime plus small business, while OppFi lends at about 130% yield to deeper subprime, and Enova's own delinquency rose.
findings.independence: This is a proxy from a different issuer. OneMain's Q3 was not found (last seen Q2 2026: consumer NCO 7.77% against 7.19% a year earlier, https://www.earningswhispers.com/epsdetails/OMF).

findings.finding: Positioning favours a relief move. Short interest built from 2.40M shares (2026-07-31) to 4.28M (2026-10-15), with days to cover up from 2.15 to 7.40 on thin turnover (average daily volume 579k). The stock is 0.4% above its 52-week low, -52% from its high, and at $5.44 trades at about 3.8x the midpoint of the cut FY adjusted-EPS guide ($1.34-1.51).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The last print into a heavy drawdown was 2026-03-11 (the stock had made a 12-month low on 2026-03-27 per MarketBeat): -5.9%. Up 5 of 7 prints overall.
findings.why_not_priced: A short of 7.4 days to cover on a closely held float is a mechanism of its own: a reaffirmed guide forces covering into thin liquidity. If the market saw no squeeze risk, days to cover would not have tripled into the print.
findings.independence: The price level comes from AAII (2026-10-27): $5.45, -9.6% in October, -47.9% YTD (https://www.aaii.com/investingideas/article/542930-why-oppfi-inc8217s-opfi-stock-is-down-501). The guide comes from the company release.

findings.finding: CEO Todd Schwartz bought in the open market during Q3 itself. He bought 60,000 shares at about $7.13 (Form 4 filed after 2026-08-13), then about 29,600 shares on nine days from 2026-09-01 to 2026-09-14 at $6.91-7.96. That is roughly $650k in total, with the quarter two weeks from closing. The stock is now $5.44, below every purchase price.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior insider-buy cluster in the baseline to compare.
findings.why_not_priced: The buys are public, but the stock fell about 30% from his last purchase price afterwards. The market has not treated the CEO's in-quarter purchases as information about Q3. If it had, the drawdown to new lows into the print would be hard to explain. The dollar amount is small against his roughly 27M-share stake.
findings.independence: Other Form 4s in the same cluster: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001818502/000090514826004133/form4.xml and https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001818502/000090514826004056/form4.xml. All are one actor, so this counts as one finding.

findings.finding: The BNCC bank acquisition is still waiting on OCC, Fed and FDIC approval, with a Q4 2026 close expected. Opposition is organised: 18 state attorneys general wrote on 2026-08-07, Senator Warren on 2026-08-14, and more than 120 advocacy groups have asked the regulators to deny it. BNCC stockholders approved the deal on 2026-09-17, and no approval has been reported. The call will update the timeline: a slip into 2027 is the likelier news given the opposition, an approval the upside.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The deal was announced on 2026-04-28 and the following print (2026-05-07) got +1.4%. Deal costs ($7.9M of Q2 transaction expense) were part of the August miss (-24.9%).
findings.why_not_priced: The opposition is public and part of the overhang. What is not public is the regulators' status. A market expecting a clean Q4 close would not have the stock at a 52-week low with the bank thesis as the bull case.
findings.independence: The AG coalition letter comes from a different source (https://insurancenewsnet.com/oarticle/attorney-general-raoul-leads-coalition-urging-federal-government-to-deny-opportunity-financial-merger, 2026-08-07). So does Warren (https://www.banking.senate.gov/newsroom/minority/warren-urges-occ-fdic-fed-to-block-a-predatory-lender-from-spreading-nationwide).

findings.finding: The line-of-credit product was the stated cause of the August guide cut. Management said then it would launch with a bank partner in September 2026, already about two months late. I found no launch announcement or press release through 2026-10-27. If it slipped again, the H2 revenue ramp the guide assumes has slipped with it.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The prior delay was disclosed with the cut guide on 2026-08-10: -24.9%.
findings.why_not_priced: A quiet launch is plausible: it is a bank-partner product in three new states and might not get a press release. So the absence of an announcement is weak evidence and is sized small. A market confident in the launch would credit the H2 guide, and the FY consensus sits at its midpoint.
findings.independence: The press-release search for September-October 2026 returned only the earnings-date notice and a conference-participation notice (https://www.placera.se/pressmeddelanden/oppfi-oppfi-announces-its-third-quarter-2026-earnings-conference-call-20261019).

findings.finding: On 2026-09-15 the company drew $75M of a new $100M senior secured multi-draw term loan at a fixed 12.50% (13.50% after the bank deal closes), with a 1.25% OID and 10% semi-annual amortisation. Stated use of proceeds: growth in finance receivables. It replaces the $75M of capacity lost when the GrayRock facility was terminated on 2026-04-15. That adds about $2.3M a quarter of interest from Q4.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No financing-driven reaction in the baseline. A $150M revolver was announced earlier with no isolated move recorded.
findings.why_not_priced: I asked what the money buys: receivables growth. Nothing corroborates a ramp, since originations were -9.3% YoY in Q2, so I read it as replacement funding at a high fixed cost rather than a demand signal. Its cost reaches the P&L from Q4 and may show in the guide. It is small against $104M of H1 free cash flow.
findings.independence: The GrayRock termination is in the Q2 presentation (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001818502/000181850226000073/a2026q2earningspresentat.htm).

outside_window.finding: A regulatory decision on the BNCC/BNC National Bank applications (OCC, Fed, FDIC) is expected around the Q4 2026 close and is unlikely to land inside the window. The opposition makes a delay or conditions more likely than not.

rejected_candidates.detail: This restates the estimate cuts already in the FY consensus and guide (bar field). It is wire content, not a separate fact.

rejected_candidates.detail: This is long-running state-law exposure that the charter strategy is built to solve. It folds into the BNCC regulatory finding, and I found no new dated event inside the window.

baseline_tension: There is no skew to agree or disagree with. Down 10.5% over 20 days, at the 52-week low, with a short that tripled its days to cover, the run-up says disappointment is largely priced. My negatives (revenue arithmetic, LOC, regulatory) agree with that drift; the positioning and insider-buy positives cut against it. The net is near zero, and the sign hangs on whether the FY guide is held.
lessons_applied: Lesson 6 (bar): the Q3 revenue bar has one source (Earnings Whispers), so I capped the revenue-arithmetic finding from -1.5 to -1.0.
Lesson 6/core (inside guide): the credit finding lands inside the already-cut FY guide, so it went from -0.5 to -0.3.
Lesson 7 (crowded short, 7.4 days to cover, short up 78% since July): I shrank the regulatory-timeline and line-of-credit negatives from -0.5 to -0.3 each.

Lesson 4 (financing): I asked what the $75M term loan buys. The answer is receivables growth that nothing corroborates, which makes it replacement funding for GrayRock. It moved from -0.3 to -0.2 and stays small.
Lesson 5 (proxy): the Enova read-across is a different customer base, so it went from +0.5 to +0.3.
Lesson 3 (caveat reaches number): the CEO buys are small against his stake, so they went from +1.0 to +0.8.
Left standing: the +1.0 positioning finding, abs_move_pct 11 and p_up 50.
